In [[mathematics]], '''Serre's modularity conjecture''', introduced by {{harvs|first=Jean-Pierre|last=Serre|authorlink=Jean-Pierre Serre|year1=1975|year2=1987|txt}}, states that an odd, [[Irreducible representation|irreducible]], two-dimensional [[Galois representation]] over a [[finite field]] arises from a [[modular form]]. A stronger version of this conjecture specifies the weight and level of the modular form. The conjecture in the level 1 case was proved by [[Chandrashekhar Khare]] in 2005,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Khare |first=Chandrashekhar |title=Serre's modularity conjecture: The level one case |year=2006 |journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]] |volume=134 |issue=3 |pages=557–589 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-06-13434-8 }}.</ref> and a proof of the full conjecture was completed jointly by Khare and [[Jean-Pierre Wintenberger]] in 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Khare |first1=Chandrashekhar |last2=Wintenberger |first2=Jean-Pierre |year=2009 |title=Serre's modularity conjecture (I) |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=178 |issue=3 |pages=485–504 |doi=10.1007/s00222-009-0205-7 |bibcode=2009InMat.178..485K }} and {{Citation |last1=Khare |first1=Chandrashekhar |last2=Wintenberger |first2=Jean-Pierre |year=2009 |title=Serre's modularity conjecture (II) |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=178 |issue=3 |pages=505–586 |doi=10.1007/s00222-009-0206-6 |bibcode=2009InMat.178..505K }}.</ref>

==Formulation==

The conjecture concerns the [[absolute Galois group]] <math>G_\mathbb{Q}</math> of the [[rational number field]] <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>.

Let <math>\rho</math> be an [[absolutely irreducible]], [[Continuous function|continuous]], two-dimensional [[Representation theory of finite groups|representation]] of <math>G_\mathbb{Q}</math> over a [[finite field]] <math>F = \mathbb{F}_{\ell^r}</math>.

:<math> \rho \colon G_\mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}_2(F).</math>

Additionally, assume <math>\rho</math> is odd, meaning the [[Image (matrix)|image]] of [[Complex conjugate|complex conjugation]] has determinant -1.

To any normalized [[modular eigenform]]

:<math> f = q+a_2q^2+a_3q^3+\cdots</math>

of [[level of a modular form|level]] <math> N=N(\rho) </math>, [[weight of a modular form|weight]] <math> k=k(\rho) </math>, and some [[Nebentype character]]

:<math> \chi \colon \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} \rightarrow F^*</math>,

a theorem due to [[Goro Shimura|Shimura]], [[Pierre Deligne|Deligne]], and Serre-Deligne attaches to <math> f </math> a representation

:<math> \rho_f\colon G_\mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}),</math>

where <math> \mathcal{O} </math> is the [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] of integers in a [[Degree of a field extension|finite extension]] of <math> \mathbb{Q}_\ell </math>. This representation is characterized by the condition that for all prime numbers <math>p</math>, [[coprime]] to <math>N\ell</math> we have

:<math> \operatorname{Trace}(\rho_f(\operatorname{Frob}_p))=a_p</math>

and

:<math> \det(\rho_f(\operatorname{Frob}_p))=p^{k-1} \chi(p).</math>

Reducing this representation [[modulo]], the [[maximal ideal]] of <math> \mathcal{O} </math> gives a mod <math> \ell </math> representation <math> \overline{\rho_f} </math> of <math> G_\mathbb{Q} </math>.

Serre's conjecture asserts that for any representation <math> \rho </math> as above, there is a modular eigenform <math> f </math> such that

:<math> \overline{\rho_f} \cong \rho </math>.

The level and weight of the conjectural form <math>f</math> are explicitly conjectured in Serre's article. In addition, he derives a number of results from this conjecture, among them [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] and the now-proven Taniyama–Weil (or Taniyama–Shimura) conjecture, now known as the [[modularity theorem]] (although this implies Fermat's Last Theorem, Serre proves it directly from his conjecture).

==Optimal level and weight==

The strong form of Serre's conjecture describes the level and weight of the modular form.

The optimal level is the [[Artin conductor]] of the representation, with the power of <math>l</math> removed.

==Proof==
A proof of the level 1 and small weight cases of the conjecture was obtained in 2004 by [[Chandrashekhar Khare]] and [[Jean-Pierre Wintenberger]], using [[P-adic L-function|P-adic L-functions]], [[Supersingular elliptic curve|supersingular elliptic curves]], and a theorem from [[Mark Kisin]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Khare |first=Chandrashekhar |last2=Wintenberger |first2=Jean-Pierre |year=2009 |title=On Serre's reciprocity conjecture for 2-dimensional mod p representations of Gal(Q/Q) |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=169 |issue=1 |pages=229–253 |doi= 10.4007/annals.2009.169.229|doi-access=free }}.</ref> Another proof was independently published by [[Luis Dieulefait]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dieulefait |first=Luis |year=2007 |title=The level 1 weight 2 case of Serre's conjecture |journal=Revista Matemática Iberoamericana |volume=23 |issue=3 |pages=1115–1124 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.rmi/1204128312 |doi=10.4171/rmi/525|arxiv=math/0412099 }}.</ref>

In 2005, Chandrashekhar Khare obtained a proof of the level 1 case of Serre conjecture,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Khare |first=Chandrashekhar |title=Serre's modularity conjecture: The level one case |year=2006 |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume=134 |issue=3 |pages=557–589 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-06-13434-8 }}.</ref> and in 2008 a proof of the full conjecture in collaboration with Jean-Pierre Wintenberger.<ref name=":0" />
